match_id: CARRICK: “IT DOESN’T MEAN EVERYTHING’S WRONG!”  Hull City_Man Utd ⚽ Premier League_2026-08-22_4HnBcj4jBh8
team: CARRICK: “IT DOESN’T MEAN EVERYTHING’S WRONG!”  Hull City
quote_text:
Hi, Michael. I know you experienced difficult  days as a player, like that defeat at Burnley in  
2009. From the dugout, was that a worse feeling  today, losing like that to newly promoted Hull? I  
wouldn’t say it’s worse. I think it’s a game  that we’ve lost, right? So it’s disappointing. Of  
course it is. You know, we came here to win, like  we do any game. So to not take anything away is  
hugely disappointing. It’s not more than that.  It’s not less than that. It’s just the one game  
that we’re disappointed we haven’t won. So we’ve  got to soak it up and come back stronger. The Hull  
manager said they were training-ground routines  they worked on Friday, the set pieces that worked  
for the goals. Was there anything that jumped  out to you that you thought was particularly  
troubling? It’s two completely different goals,  really, so it’s not time to dissect it as such.  
I think we’ve been pretty good over a period  of time. Today they’ve obviously scored two  
in different ways, so I understand why that’s  highlighted. But it happens sometimes. It happens  
in football, but we don’t accept it. It happens,  and we’ve got to understand why. I know there’s  
a lot of noise around United and it’s easy to get  carried away. There always is. Yeah, yeah. How do  
you sum that up? Because I think your team were  more passive than people expected. I know you  
said this was going to be a tough challenge, but  I don’t think anybody expected Hull to win. No,  
but that doesn’t mean you’re passive just  because you get beat. The result’s the result, so  
we accept it. We got beat. We’re hurting. It’s not  a nice feeling at all. It doesn’t mean it’s going  
to change the whole direction of how we’re going  as a team or as a football club. It’s one game,  
and results can happen in football. We all  understand that. It’s not nice when they do,  
but it does happen. We can be better. We will be  better. There are things we can be much better  
at. There are things that were actually all right  that get lost in the game because you get beat.  
But I understand that as well. Michael,  most people have said that your calmness,  
winning and losing, is one of the key attributes  for you dealing with this job. But do you also  
understand that games like that generate a huge  amount of debate and negativity, and people expect  
a kind of reaction from you, even though that’s  not your general demeanour or approach? I know  
there’s a lot that goes on outside of our football  club. I understand the responsibility I’ve got,  
but it doesn’t make me do things differently just  because of that. Hi, Michael. Do you feel like  
the system is having some issues against teams  that play with a back five? Thinking back to the  
Leeds game, 2-1 at Old Trafford, obviously  AC Milan last weekend. Is it a coincidence,  
obviously Hull today, or do you think there’s  something potentially there? We haven’t lost many  
games in six or seven months. Again, I get it.  We’ve lost today and I understand it, and there  
are questions to be asked, but it doesn’t mean  everything’s wrong because we’ve lost the game.  
We’ve done a lot of good things and we did  some good things today, but it gets lost,  
and I understand it’ll get lost. But it doesn’t  get lost from our point of view. So yeah, there  
are definitely issues playing against different  systems, so we’ve got to find the answers for  
that. But just because we lose one game doesn’t  mean that everything needs dissected and it’s  
wrong from our point of view. I understand from  others it happens, and that’s how it is. Could  
you explain Patrick Dorgu’s position when going  forward? Obviously, he’s taking up a few central  
positions. Having subbed him at half-time, do you  think he might need an arm around him this week?  
No, purely. Pat’s fine. We love him to bits. He’s  a fantastic player, Pat. He’s a great character,  
he’s a big part of what we do and he will  be. It was just one of those decisions. It’s  
nothing personal. Sometimes you’ve just got to  make them, trying to do something a little bit  
different. Do you find it easy in these situations  to remain quite calm? Obviously, it’s part of your  
personality, but you’ve mentioned the noise and  what people will say after this. Do you find it  
quite easy just to put your foot on the ball  a little bit and say, look, we don’t need to  
[inaudible] one game, we move on? It depends how  you see calmness. I’ve talked to you quite calmly,  
but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying  the day. There’s a big difference. I played  
here for a long time. You don’t get to play here  for a long time without just going day by day.  
There are ups and downs, but you just carry on as  normal. It’s 100 per cent not that, and trust me,  
it’s not that. It just doesn’t mean that we  all have to shout and scream and come out and  
create some chaos just because of it.  Inside we’re hurting. The boys know,  
and we need to get better. The calmness doesn’t  mean that there’s no emotion in it, for sure. Hi,  
Michael. You played six games in pre-season with  a lot of good points from what you saw. How big  
a shock today was the defeat and the manner of  it? Yeah, we got beat by two set plays. The goals  
are the goals, and pre-season’s pre-season as  well. Whatever way it goes and whatever happens,  
the season’s a season in itself. I’m not sure I  can remember too many pre-seasons, whether we’ve  
had success or not. So it puts you at a starting  point to then make the next step. We’ve lost a  
game. We have lost one game, and it’s not a nice  one to lose, the first game of the season. But it  
won’t change what we do and how we move forward.  Was there anything that you saw in pre-season, in  
terms of... Say again? Was there anything that you  saw in pre-season that might have prepared you for  
what happened today, in terms of warning signs?  There are always things that happen all the time,  
things that we see that we like. Sometimes we see  little habits or patterns that we want to improve  
on. That’s fine. But just because we lost the game  today, we don’t have to dissect the whole picture  
because it’s definitely not bad. Not meaning  to dissect this, but I think you had four or  
five goalscorers on the pitch at the end, with  Rashford, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha and Šeško all  
on the pitch. Can you put your finger on why that  didn’t necessarily click and put more pressure on  
the Hull goal? Yeah, listen, we changed things  around a little bit in the second half and we  
kept trying to find a different way, a little  bit of finding a spark. It happens. It does  
happen. It has happened before. We’ve just got  to keep finding those solutions. Ben’s been out  
for quite some time and hasn’t trained an awful  lot, so there are little bits of reasons for it.  
Bryan’s been really good for a lot of pre-season  and was one of our better players again today.
